commitResults.messageBody:
Merge upstream master into partial-name search

Upstream master adds supporter fields, stages and interactions.
Integrate these changes so the find/list feature stays compatible.

Resolve conflicts while preserving partial-name matching and
upstream feature documentation. Fix the Messages line-length issue.

Startup loading falls back to an empty supporter list when data cannot
be read, but the failure is recorded only in the log.

Retain a warning describing the data path and overwrite risk so it can
be displayed when the UI starts. Preserve valid-file and first-launch
loading behavior, and verify that startup leaves the data untouched.

Users see an empty supporter list after a loading failure without an
explanation in the application window.

Pass initial feedback from startup loading to the result display and
wrap its text so the overwrite advice remains readable. Keep normal
command feedback and saving behavior, and retain existing UI entry
points for launches without a warning.

Validation: Gradle checks and isolated JavaFX startup smoke tests pass.

The guides do not describe the visible startup warning, and the User
Guide names an outdated supporter data file path.

Explain missing, valid and unreadable data-file launches, including
how to preserve data before continuing. Document the warning's UI
handoff and add manual checks for startup and later command feedback.

Limit these updates to loading and saving documentation so other
feature sections remain intact.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report interaction counts when deleting supporters
commitResults.messageBody:
Deletion removes a supporter's embedded interaction history but does
not tell the user how many entries were removed.

Report the count on a second line of the success message and clarify
the command usage. Verify empty, single, multiple and duplicate
interaction histories without changing existing deletion behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Verify deletion preserves filters and viewed state
commitResults.messageBody:
Deletion must use displayed indices, retain the active find filter,
and keep other supporters' histories and viewed selection intact.

Exercise deletion through the parser, model and JSON storage. Check
that deleting the viewed supporter clears selection and that failed
commands preserve the displayed list, selection and saved file.

Reload saved data to verify the deleted history is absent and notes
on other supporters, including references to the deleted name, remain.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document supporter deletion and history removal
commitResults.messageBody:
The delete documentation does not describe interaction-count feedback
or the effects on filtering and viewed selection.

Explain the two-line result, permanent history removal and preserved
filter and unrelated data. Document the existing selection behavior
and add manual deletion and reload checks, without claiming that a
detail panel is already present.

Phone numbers accept digits only, preventing users from entering country
codes and readable separators.

Allow an optional leading plus sign and single spaces or hyphens between
digit groups, including mixed separators. Preserve entered formatting
and retain the 3 to 15 digit limit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move phone limit comment beside its constants
commitResults.messageBody:
The digit-limit comment sits above the formatting regex even though
separate constants define the allowed number of digits.

Move the comment above those constants so its placement reflects the
validation responsibilities.
Allow country codes and separators in phone numbers

Name-only matching cannot express searches across supporter details.

Add matching criteria for names, organisations, tags, stages, phones and
emails. Combine alternatives within each field using OR and different
fields using AND so users can narrow their searches.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support field filters in the find command
commitResults.messageBody:
Find accepts only name keywords, leaving other supporter details
unavailable as search criteria.

Parse field prefixes alongside name keywords and apply combined
matching. Reject empty criteria and invalid stages so malformed searches
produce useful feedback.

Expanded searches change the displayed list used by indexed commands.

Add integration coverage for displayed indices, replacement filters,
viewed selection and undo history to protect existing workflows.

The User Guide describes name-only searches.

Document field prefixes, combined matching and formatting-independent
phone searches. Explain keyword placement and provide examples so users
can predict which supporters a search will return.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support sorting the displayed supporter list
commitResults.messageBody:
Filtered supporter lists preserve insertion order, so commands cannot
prioritize relationships by their last-contact date.

Add a sorted view over the filtered list without reordering stored data.
Restore insertion order for ordinary filters and retain source order for
ties so displayed indices remain predictable.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add quiet command for inactive supporters
commitResults.messageBody:
Staff need to identify relationships that have gone without contact.

Add quiet with a default threshold of 60 days and an optional positive
day count. Include never-contacted supporters, exclude Declined stages
and show the longest silence first using the latest interaction date.

Quiet changes the displayed order used by commands that take indices.

Test indexed updates, live filtering, restored ordering, saved data and
undo history so prioritizing supporters preserves existing workflows.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document quiet supporter filtering and ordering
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides do not explain how to identify supporters needing follow-up.

Document quiet thresholds, ordering, exclusions and displayed indices.
Explain how normal ordering is restored and how the sorted view keeps
stored supporter data unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover search predicate equality and diagnostics
commitResults.messageBody:
Patch coverage misses diagnostic output and comparisons where only one
search field differs, leaving the Codecov check below its target.

Test each field independently and verify equality after normalization.
Check the diagnostic output so every predicate branch is covered.

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete quiet coverage and convention checks
commitResults.messageBody:
Sorted-list equality has an untested differing-order branch, and test
helpers use noun-only names.

Verify both equality outcomes and rename helpers to describe their
actions. Keep the new feature fully covered and consistent with the
Java naming conventions.
Find supporters by other fields

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve quiet order when contact dates tie
commitResults.messageBody:
Quiet sorting compares only last-contact dates. Replacing a
supporter after a tag change can move them within an equal-date group,
even though their contact history and full-list position are unchanged.

Use each supporter's current full-list position to break date ties.
Keep displayed indices predictable without changing stored order.

Add regression tests for tag updates among never-contacted supporters
and supporters with equal contact dates, including untagging and a log
that creates a new date tie. Document the explicit ordering guarantee
in the Developer Guide.

Quiet filtering and sorting have no dedicated execution diagram, making
the display-view updates harder to follow from the guide alone.

Add a focused sequence diagram for QuietCommand, ModelManager and the
filtered and sorted lists. Explain eligibility, full-list tie-breaking
and result counting without repeating generic parsing or persistence.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain quiet sequence diagram in developer guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The quiet execution diagram is not referenced from the Developer Guide.

Embed it beside the quiet implementation description and explain its
scope and omitted interactions. Keep the diagram close to the behaviour
it illustrates so future developers can relate the prose to the model.

The diagram repeats rules already explained in the guide. Placing the
note after the result return can suggest work happens after execution.

Replace it with a short note beside the filter and sort updates.
Align the DG introduction with the revised diagram to avoid repetition
and keep the execution sequence clear.
Document quiet execution with a sequence diagram

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject null tags when loading supporter data
commitResults.messageBody:
A null entry in a saved tag list raises an unchecked exception and
prevents the normal startup recovery path from running.

Reject the entry as an invalid saved value so storage can report a
data-loading failure. Keep absent and empty tag lists valid for
existing files, and cover both behaviours with adapter tests.

Refs #154

commitResults.messageTitle: Verify startup recovery for null-tag data
commitResults.messageBody:
Adapter validation alone does not prove that a malformed tag reaches
the existing empty-list and startup-warning behaviour.

Exercise the reported JSON through storage and application startup.
Check that the warning identifies the unreadable file and that loading
leaves its bytes unchanged so the user can still recover the data.

Fixes #154

Valid contact details with parenthesized digit groups, type labels or
extensions cannot be recorded without removing useful information.

Accept balanced digit groups, an optional one-to-six-digit extension
and an optional alphabetic label while preserving the entered value.
Apply the three-to-fifteen-digit limit only to the main number and
reject malformed annotations through the normal validation messages.

Cover model validation, add/edit parsing and storage round trips so
the accepted format stays consistent across entry and persistence.

Refs #152

commitResults.messageTitle: Support annotated numbers in phone searches
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone searches remove only the old separators, so accepting new
annotations without updating search would make stored contacts harder
to find and reject queries copied from the displayed phone number.

Share phone syntax with search validation while allowing short search
fragments. Ignore digit-group parentheses, labels and extension markers
when matching, but retain extension digits in substring searches.

Verify add, edit, find, undo/redo and saved formatting through logic,
including invalid inputs that must leave the previous state unchanged.

Refs #152

The guides describe only digit groups separated by spaces or hyphens,
which no longer explains the accepted annotations or search behaviour.

Describe parenthesized groups, alphabetic labels and bounded extensions.
Clarify which digits count towards the number limit and which parts are
ignored in searches. Include examples and manual regression steps for
entry, editing, searching and persistence.

Fixes #152

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn when added supporters share contact details
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding a differently named supporter with an existing phone or email
only confirms success, making possible duplicate records easy to miss.

Append an advisory warning naming every matching existing supporter
and the shared fields. Compare complete normalized phone numbers and
case-insensitive emails across the full address book, not just the
displayed results. Preserve extension boundaries in phone comparisons.

Keep additions allowed because households and organisations may share
contact details. Leave name-based duplicate rejection unchanged.

Refs #148

A warning must not turn a legitimate shared contact into a blocked
addition, alter existing supporters or create extra undo history.

Exercise the reported examples through command parsing and storage.
Verify hidden matches, unchanged success feedback without matches,
absence of self-warnings and a single undoable addition. Check that
duplicate names and invalid contacts remain rejected without losing
saved data or redo history.

Refs #148

Users need to know that an advisory contact match does not mean the
addition failed or that two supporters necessarily represent one person.

Explain warning scope, full-number and email matching, hidden records
and unchanged duplicate-name validation. Document the implementation
and manual checks for shared contacts, filtering and undo/redo.

Fixes #148

commitResults.messageTitle: Order phone regex constants by dependency
commitResults.messageBody:
The combined phone regex precedes its component constants and needs
class-qualified references, making the validation rules harder to read
from top to bottom.

Move the combined regex below its components and use their plain names.
Keep the public constant and accepted phone formats unchanged while
making the dependency order explicit.

Refs #152

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve supporter selection across rename history
commitResults.messageBody:
Undo and redo currently look up the viewed supporter by name, which
clears the detail panel when a rename is undone even though the
supporter still exists.

Track immutable record versions by their original object identity so
selection follows the same supporter independently of names and list
indices. Release unused metadata after no-op edits and discarded redo
branches, without changing the saved-data format.

Cover repeated edits, reused names, shifted indices, failed edits and
branched history with model regression tests.

Fixes #179

commitResults.messageTitle: Verify viewed supporter history through commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Exercise the reported filtered rename sequence through LogicManager,
including undo, redo, a new history branch and persisted data. Check
that renaming an introducer also preserves a viewed dependent and
that undoing an addition still clears the missing supporter.

Document session-only record lineage and metadata cleanup so future
developers do not replace it with name or displayed-index matching.

Related to #179

The repeated alternatives in the name expression exhaust the JVM
stack on sufficiently long names. Data accepted and saved by the app
can therefore prevent a later launch from loading the same file.

Match whole slash words before individual characters and use
possessive repetition to avoid recursive backtracking. Preserve the
existing naming rules without adding an arbitrary length limit.

Test long valid and invalid names, including slash-word boundaries.

Fixes #182

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject null entries in saved supporter data
commitResults.messageBody:
A null supporter entry bypasses field validation and triggers an
uncaught exception instead of the documented loading fallback.

Reject null records before converting supporters, and verify that
null roots and null entries produce DataLoadingException without
changing the original file. Include a valid record before a null
entry to prevent partially loaded data from escaping validation.

Fixes #180

commitResults.messageTitle: Verify long names survive saving and reloading
commitResults.messageBody:
Exercise long names through add, edit, undo, redo and JSON reloading.
Check that invalid edits still fail and that startup loads a saved

Document the packaged-app reproduction so release testing includes

Related to #182

commitResults.messageTitle: Verify null data uses the startup fallback
commitResults.messageBody:
Check the complete startup path for null roots, null supporters and

Add manual checks to the Developer Guide so the warning and safe

Related to #180

commitResults.messageBody:
Remove the general claim about preserved formats and length limits

Keep the expected result focused on observable behavior: adding the

No application code or tests are changed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Flag prefixes outside the current command format
commitResults.messageBody:
The prefix advisory recognizes every SupporterBook prefix globally.
Prefixes belonging to other commands therefore produce misleading
field errors or are saved inside note text without an explanation.

Check prefix-like words against the current command's format and
clarify that recognition is command-specific. Preserve literal text,
ordinary slash words and the existing parsing-versus-execution error
distinction. Ignore extra arguments for commands that already do so.

Cover command formats, ordered warnings and exemptions with focused
prefix-detection tests.

Fixes #198

Exercise the three reported commands through LogicManager so both
parsing errors and successful saves identify unsupported prefixes.
Check saved note text, undo/redo, execution errors and preservation
of selection, filters and files after a parsing failure.

Update the guides to explain command-specific recognition and add
observable manual checks for prefixes used in the wrong command.

Related to #198

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn about shared contacts after edits
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding a supporter warns about shared contact details, but editing
can introduce the same phone or email without any warning.

Reuse the existing full-number and case-insensitive email comparison
for the edited record. Exclude the original supporter from the full
list so hidden matches are included without reporting a self-match.
Keep the warning advisory and use update-specific success wording.

Test matching contacts, renamed supporters, hidden matches and
unchanged normal feedback when no other supporter matches.

Fixes #200

commitResults.messageBody:
Check the reported sample-data cases through command parsing and
persistence. Cover filtered lists, selection, undo/redo, no-op edits,

Document advisory edit warnings and add manual checks that compare

Related to #200

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge upstream master into prefix-warning branch
commitResults.messageBody:
Master now rejects unsupported known prefixes in find directly,
and includes other parser and validation updates made since this
branch was published.

Bring those changes into the prefix-warning branch so the follow-up
can account for explicit search-filter errors. Preserve the existing
published history rather than rewriting the reviewed commits.

Related to #198

Find now rejects known unsupported prefixes itself. The advisory
scan also flags those prefixes, adding a contradictory explanation
that they were read as ordinary text. An existing integration test
also assumes that a search using n/ still succeeds.

Use the global prefix set for find advisories so only unknown words
receive a note. Preserve explicit filter errors and update the
read-only search test to use x/ instead of n/.

Add regression coverage for unsupported filters, mixed known and
unknown prefixes, and unchanged data and selection after rejection.
Clarify the find exception in both guides.

Address review feedback on PR #208 after merging PR #211.

Search, quiet and deletion paths lack local assertions and diagnostic
logging, making internal contract violations harder to investigate.

Assert search membership, quiet ordering, deletion cleanup and valid
normalized criteria. Add FINE-level summaries containing counts rather
than supporter details or search text, without replacing input checks.

Test deliberately broken model contracts and verify the diagnostic
messages. Keep assertion checks enabled in the test run.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document field searches and quiet workflows
commitResults.messageBody:
UC03 describes only name searches, and the DG has no quiet use case or
dedicated manual tests despite supporting both workflows.

Extend UC03 to cover field alternatives, combined criteria and errors.
Add UC14 for quiet thresholds, exclusions, ordering and preserved state.

Document an isolated manual-test sequence with relative dates, boundary
checks, displayed indices, live updates, undo/redo and saved order.
Use disposable data and explicit setup to keep results reliable.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover lower ASCII bound in phone assertions
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone-criterion tests cover empty values and characters above '9', but
not the lower ASCII digit boundary.

Add 91.23 so its period makes the digit >= '0' condition evaluate to
false. Rename the test to include invalid criteria that contain digits.

Exercise the previously missed branch without changing phone validation.
Add search diagnostics and document quiet workflows
Remove leftover AB3 placeholders from DG manual tests

Very long formatted numbers exhaust the regex matcher's stack before
the main-number digit limit is checked. Search fragments share the
same matcher, and invalid saved numbers bypass normal load recovery.

Use possessive repetition for unambiguous digit groups and label words
without changing phone syntax or search-fragment length rules. Cover
long additions, edits, searches and saved data alongside annotations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make email validation safe for long inputs
commitResults.messageBody:
Repeated dot-separated local parts exhaust the matcher stack, while
the domain pattern rejects consecutive internal hyphens and ASCII
internationalised domain names.

Use possessive repetition for delimiter-separated words and domain
labels. Accept internal hyphen runs while keeping label boundaries,
local-part dot rules and the two-character final-label requirement.

Cover long valid and invalid inputs, command rejection without data
changes, and saving and reloading accepted emails. Preserve the
existing absence of an email length limit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject trailing content in saved JSON
commitResults.messageBody:
Reading only the first JSON value silently accepts concatenated books
or malformed trailing text. A later save discards that ignored data
without the documented startup warning.

Check for the end of the input after deserializing one value and reject
extra tokens through the existing loading-error path. Keep trailing
whitespace and unknown fields inside the object supported.

Verify utility and storage rejection, unchanged source files and
startup recovery with an explicit warning instead of partial data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match Unicode case variants in substring searches
commitResults.messageBody:
Whole-string lowercasing changes Greek final sigma according to its
position and expands dotted I. Lowercasing search terms separately
therefore misses exact substrings and names considered identical.

Fold individual Unicode code points using the same simple case
comparison as name identity. Preserve canonical normalization,
apostrophe handling, accents and the original stored spelling.

Cover Greek sigma, dotted and dotless I, supplementary letters and
predicate equality through model tests and real command searches.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse stages independently of the default locale
commitResults.messageBody:
Turkish uppercasing changes giving into an unknown enum name even
though validation accepts it. Valid commands then fail unexpectedly,
and previously saved supporters cannot load at startup.

Select stages with the same case-insensitive comparison as validation
instead of converting input with the default locale. Format labels
with the root locale so stored and displayed stage names stay stable.

Cover every stage, Unicode I variants, command parsing, saved-data
round trips and startup without a spurious loading warning.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align contact rules with validation and warnings
commitResults.messageBody:
The add section incorrectly says shared-contact warnings do not apply
to edits, contradicting the edit section and the implemented workflow.

Describe warnings for both additions and edits, while keeping loading
outside that check. Clarify email domain boundaries, internal hyphens
and ASCII internationalised domain names alongside the existing rules.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document Unicode case folding in search
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide still describes Locale.ROOT lowercasing, which no
longer matches the Unicode substring-search implementation.

Describe per-code-point upper-then-lower case folding and illustrate
Greek sigma and dotted I matching. Keep the existing guarantees about
canonical normalization, significant accents and unchanged stored text.

Refs #271

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to delete logged interactions
commitResults.messageBody:
Interaction history supports logging entries but has no command to
remove an entry recorded by mistake.

Add UnlogCommand to delete an interaction by its displayed number,
report the removed entry and select the updated supporter. Preserve
other supporter details, remaining interactions and the list filter.

Use chronological numbering to match the detail panel while targeting
an exact stored position so identical interactions remain distinct.
Reject invalid indices without changing data or selection.

Add command tests covering chronological targeting, duplicate entries,
empty history, field preservation, filtered lists and failure behavior.
Parser routing and documentation will follow in separate commits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to edit logged interactions
commitResults.messageBody:
Interaction history supports recording entries but has no command to
correct a recorded note or date.

Add EditLogCommand to edit an interaction by its displayed number,
preserve omitted fields and report its updated chronological number.
Keep other supporter details, remaining interactions and the list
filter unchanged, and select the updated supporter on success.

Retain the entry's stored position to preserve equal-date ordering and
target identical interactions independently. Reject invalid indices
without changing data or selection.

Add tests for partial and combined edits, date reordering, equal-date
ties, identical entries, field preservation and failure behavior.
All 17 command tests and both Checkstyle checks pass.
Parser routing and documentation will follow in separate commits.

UnlogCommand can delete an interaction, but command input does not yet
reach it. Users need a way to select the supporter and interaction to
remove through the command box.

Add UnlogCommandParser and route unlog input through AddressBookParser.
Reuse the shared two-index parser to keep index validation consistent,
and report invalid arguments with the unlog usage message.

Add tests for valid input, whitespace, missing or extra arguments,
invalid indices and command routing. Include the blank-line cleanup in
UnlogCommand.equals to separate its logical sections.

Parser, routing and command tests and both Checkstyle checks pass.

EditLogCommand supports correcting interactions, but command input does
not yet reach it. Users need to identify an entry and supply a note,
a date or both while leaving omitted fields unchanged.

Add EditLogCommandParser and route editlog through AddressBookParser.
Reuse shared index, note and date validation to keep behavior consistent
with existing commands. Require at least one edit field, accept either
prefix order and reject repeated prefixes.

Command and parser tests cover interaction edits separately, but do not
verify that updated display numbers can target subsequent edits.

Add integration tests from command text through the model to detail-panel
data. Verify date reordering, edits using refreshed numbers, equal-date
ordering and targeting of identical entries. Check that supporter details,
selection and filtering are preserved.

The new integration tests and related command and parser tests pass,
along with both Checkstyle checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Verify unlog behavior through detail-panel data
commitResults.messageBody:
Command and parser tests cover deletion separately, but do not verify
that displayed interaction numbers remain usable across commands.

Add integration tests from command text through the model to detail-panel
data. Verify chronological targeting, renumbering across consecutive
deletions, identical entries and the empty-history state. Check that
supporter details, selection and filtering are preserved.

Group display-history assertions in a helper and name snapshots by their
deletion step to keep the sequential workflow easy to follow.

All three integration tests and both Checkstyle checks pass.
